page: Google Cloud Platform c3-standard-4-lssd is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the c3 server family. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8481C processor operating at 2.7 GHz. The system is equipped with 16 GB of RAM, providing a 4.0 GB per core ratio, and includes a bundled 402 GB local NVMe SSD. The x86_64 architecture supports advanced instruction sets, including Intel Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for deep learning and matrix operations, alongside cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA_NI.

Benchmark results indicate a performance profile that is generally average in single-threaded tasks but weaker in multi-threaded and memory-intensive workloads. The single-core stress-ng and Geekbench scores fall into the average category, as does single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression. However, multi-core performance is weak, as demonstrated by the stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core benchmarks. Memory bandwidth is also limited, with both read and write large-block tests registering in the weak category. Static web serving throughput remains average at 6.5 GB/sec.

The inclusion of a 402 GB local NVMe SSD provides high-speed local storage, which offsets the weaker memory bandwidth and multi-core processing constraints for workloads requiring fast disk access. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this instance offers a balanced resource density for workloads that do not fully saturate multi-threaded CPU capacity but benefit from dedicated compute resources and local storage. Appropriate workloads include static web serving, lightweight database operations, text processing, and single-threaded utility tasks.
